{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement — verified findings

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against 19 playbook rules. The document is unusually well aligned with our positions: 17 of 19 rules are compliant, including the critical indemnification (§ 20) and IP/Customer Data ownership (§ 14) rules, and the high-severity assignment/change-of-control (§ 24), licence grant (§ 13), termination-for-convenience (§ 9.4) and no-exclusivity/no-non-compete positions (§ 12.3). Several clauses run affirmatively in our favour, notably the Vendor-granted MFN (§ 7.6), Vendor's non-compete covenant (§ 12.4), the audit protections (§ 22.2–22.3), transition assistance priced at expiring Order Form rates (§ 11) and the CPI/3% renewal uplift cap (§ 8.3). None of these require redlining.

Two deviations remain, and both sit in walk-away territory notwithstanding their low playbook severity ranking:

1. **§ 7.7 — Customer-payable liquidated damages.** A late-payment charge of 15% of annual Fees per week, triggered by a ten-day payment delay, would exceed the remaining contract value in roughly seven weeks. This fails the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties) and cannot be brought within the fallback, which covers only an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.
2. **§ 21.1 — Illusory liability cap.** The cap structure is otherwise acceptable and mutual, with sound Excluded Claims in § 21.3, but the cap base is defined "Fees", which § 1.5 limits to the "Implementation Fee" — a one-time USD 12,000 charge under § 1.6, further narrowed by § 21.1 to the first Order Form. Recurring subscription and services charges are excluded, leaving an effective cap of USD 12,000, far below our six-month floor.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 (with § 21.3) |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14 (with §§ 13.2, 15.1) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 (12.3; § 2.1) |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 12 (12.3) |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9 (9.4; § 29.4) |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 |
| Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | Compliant | § 7 (7.6, in our favour) |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 2 (2.1; §§ 7.1, 12) |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 (12.3) |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8 |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19 (with § 6) |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 |
| Low | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 (7.7) |
| Low | LOL-CAP — Liability cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 21 (21.1) |

## Walk-away items

Both open deviations are identified in our findings as walk-away territory and should be treated as gating rather than trade-able:

- **§ 7.7 liquidated damages.** At 15% of annual Fees per week for a ten-day payment delay, exposure exceeds the remaining contract value within approximately seven weeks. No comparable Customer-payable liquidated damages or early-termination sums appear elsewhere (termination under §§ 9.4 and 10 carries none), so this is a discrete fix.
- **§ 21.1 cap base.** An effective USD 12,000 cap is below our six-month floor and is functionally no cap at all. The mutuality in § 21.1, the mutual consequential-damages exclusion in § 21.2 and the Excluded Claims in § 21.3 are acceptable and should be preserved as drafted.

## Next steps

1. **Send two redlines only.** We propose flipping § 7.7 so that no liquidated damages or penalty are payable by Customer for late payment, substituting simple interest on undisputed overdue amounts — this preserves Vendor's remedy and is consistent with the interest reference in § 7.3. For § 21.1, we propose resetting the cap basis to the greater of all amounts paid or payable in the preceding twelve months or USD 1,000,000, leaving mutuality and the § 21.3 carve-outs untouched.
2. **Re-draft and re-verify the § 21.1 redline before it goes out.** Automated verification of that proposal returned a failure, so the drafting needs a manual pass to confirm it correctly displaces the § 1.5/§ 1.6 "Fees"/Implementation Fee definition and the first-Order-Form limitation. The § 7.7 proposal verified after repair and is ready subject to a read-through.
3. **Consider a conforming definitional fix.** Because the § 21.1 problem originates in the § 1.5 definition of "Fees" (read with § 1.6), we should decide whether to fix the cap language in place or amend the definition; either route must ensure recurring subscription and services charges are captured in the cap base.
4. **Confirm no further trades are needed.** The remaining 17 rules are compliant and require no comment, so we can present this as a short, two-issue markup and hold both items as conditions to signature.
"}
